name: Linet-Tian Static Cylinder
description: The static vacuum field with cylindrical symmetry and a cosmological constant, the field outside an infinitely long straight line of mass, which Bernard Linet and Qingjun Tian found independently in 1986. With a negative constant it approaches anti-de Sitter space far from its axis; with a positive one the proper distance from the axis is bounded by $\pi/\sqrt{3\Lambda}$, and the surfaces of constant distance are tori.
convention: The exponents $p_0$, $p_2$, and $p_3$ are those of Levi-Civita's cylinder in proper distance, with $p_0 + p_2 + p_3 = p_0^2 + p_2^2 + p_3^2 = 1$, and every component assumes both conditions. We keep factors of $c$ explicit, and the Ricci tensor is the standard contraction, $R_{\mu\nu} = R^\alpha{}_{\mu\alpha\nu}$.
history: The static vacuum around an infinitely long straight line of mass, in a universe with a cosmological constant $\Lambda$, depends only on the proper distance $\rho$ from the axis. Its line element is $ds^2 = d\rho^2 + Q^{2/3}\left(-P^{2p_t}c^2dt^2 + P^{2p_z}dz^2 + P^{2p_\phi}d\phi^2/C^2\right)$, where $Q = \sin(\sqrt{3\Lambda}\,\rho)/\sqrt{3\Lambda}$ and $P = 2\tan(\sqrt{3\Lambda}\,\rho/2)/\sqrt{3\Lambda}$ [dasilva2000, zofka2008]. The exponents are $p_t = -(4\sigma^2 - 8\sigma + 1)/(3\Sigma)$, $p_z = (8\sigma^2 - 4\sigma - 1)/(3\Sigma)$, and $p_\phi = -2(2\sigma^2 + 2\sigma - 1)/(3\Sigma)$, where $\Sigma = 4\sigma^2 - 2\sigma + 1$ [dasilva2000]. Near the axis and as $\Lambda \to 0$ both $Q$ and $P$ tend to $\rho$, and the metric becomes the static cylinder of Tullio Levi-Civita, with $\sigma$ his mass parameter and $C$ its conicity [dasilva2000, griffiths2010linettian]. For a negative $\Lambda$ the sine and the tangent become hyperbolic functions of $\sqrt{3|\Lambda|}\,\rho$ [dasilva2000, zofka2008]. With $\Lambda \neq 0$ the Weyl tensor vanishes for no member, so de Sitter and anti-de Sitter space, which are conformally flat, are not among them [dasilva2000, griffiths2010linettian].¶Bernard Linet in Paris and Qingjun Tian in Chicago found these solutions independently, each to describe the field outside a cosmic string [zofka2008, linet1986, tian1986]. Linet's paper was received in October 1985 and Tian's that December [linet1986, tian1986]. Tian wrote that "all static and cylindrically symmetric vacuum solutions of Einstein's field equation with cosmological constant" are found [tian1986]. Andrzej Krasiński had given empty space fields with a cosmological constant in 1975, as exteriors for a rotating perfect fluid, with a cross term between time and the angle about the axis [krasinski1975]. Reinaldo Gleiser showed in 2021 that one of Krasiński's four types becomes static under a linear change of its Killing vectors and is then the Linet-Tian family [gleiser2021krasinski, krasinski1975]. Krasiński had left the static case aside, writing that the generalisation of the static vacuum to a nonzero $\Lambda$ is "unexpectedly very involved" [krasinski1975].¶Eugênio Ramos Bezerra de Mello, Yves Brihaye, and Betti Hartmann recovered the vacuum field with a positive constant and a boost along the axis in 2003, and calculated the field of a self gravitating cosmic string numerically [mello2003strings]. Sourav Bhattacharya and Amitabha Lahiri built a model with a finite string core in 2008 and calculated how the constant changes the angle deficit and the bending of light [bhattacharya2008strings]. Amir M. Abbassi, Saeed Mirshekari, and Amir H. Abbassi compared seven prescriptions for the energy of the static cosmic string the same year [abbassi2008energy]. Bhattacharya calculated the one loop correction from quantum electrodynamics to photon propagation in this member in 2015 and found opposite velocity shifts for its two transverse polarizations, for radial and azimuthal motion [bhattacharya2015photons].¶With a negative constant the metric is regular everywhere away from the axis, and far from it every member approaches anti-de Sitter space in horospherical coordinates [zofka2008, dasilva2000, tian1986]. Maria de Fátima da Silva, Anzhong Wang, Filipe Paiva, and Nilton Santos showed in 2000 that the axis is singular for every $\sigma$ except $0$ and $1/2$, as in Levi-Civita's field [dasilva2000]. Martin Žofka and Jiří Bičák built nonsingular cylindrical shells as sources of the field in 2008 [zofka2008]. With $\Lambda < 0$, $\sigma = 0$, and $C = 1$ the axis is regular too, and the spacetime has no singularity anywhere [bronnikov2020, sarioglu2009comment]. William Bonnor described this member in 2008 as a second anti-de Sitter universe, "static, cylindrically symmetric and of Petrov class D" [bonnor2008second]. Özgür Sarıoğlu and Bayram Tekin identified it with the soliton of anti-de Sitter space found by Gary Horowitz and Robert Myers, through a change of radius that Roberto Emparan suggested [sarioglu2009comment, horowitz1998].¶Sarıoğlu and Tekin carried the family with a negative constant to every higher dimension in 2009, with exponents whose sum and whose sum of squares are both $1$ [sarioglu2009higher]. Of all those spacetimes the soliton alone has no naked singularity, with its circle given the period that removes a conical singularity [sarioglu2009higher]. Jerry Griffiths and Jiří Podolský gave the field with a positive constant in any higher number of dimensions in 2010 [griffiths2010linettian]. Griffiths and Santos built a rotating source for the field with a negative constant the same year: a rigidly rotating cylinder of dust whose interior is the universe of Kurt Gödel, with an exterior that is locally the static field for a small enough product of the rotation and the radius of the cylinder [griffiths2010rotating]. Past a second, larger value of that product the exterior reaches a region with closed timelike curves [griffiths2010rotating].¶A positive constant gives $\rho$ a finite range, from $0$ to $\pi/\sqrt{3\Lambda}$, and the far end is a second curvature singularity unless $\sigma$ is $-1/2$, $1/4$, or $1$ [dasilva2000, griffiths2010linettian]. Griffiths and Podolský showed in 2010 that $z$ is then periodic like $\phi$, so every surface of constant $\rho$ is a torus, and each singular end is a closed axis with its own conicity [griffiths2010linettian]. They replaced one singular axis with a toroidal region of the Einstein static universe full of dust, matched to the vacuum across a torus [griffiths2010linettian]. The dust then has a mass per unit length of $\sigma(1 - \sigma)/(1 - 4\sigma^2)$, approximately $\sigma$ for small values [griffiths2010linettian]. Reflected about the middle of the range of $\rho$, with $\phi$ and $z$ exchanged and $C = 1$, the metric with $\sigma$ becomes the one with $(1 - 4\sigma)/(4(1 - \sigma))$, so its far axis carries a source of that strength [griffiths2010linettian]. For a positive constant Tian found three exteriors of a string: a universe with a curvature singularity, one with a conical singularity, and one with no singularity [tian1986].¶Irene Brito and coauthors matched static elastic interiors to the field for either sign of the constant in 2012 [brito2012elastic]. Brito, da Silva, Filipe Mena, and Santos proved in 2013 that no static, conformally flat interior with a regular axis matches smoothly to the field with $\Lambda < 0$, and with $\Lambda > 0$ they matched two such interiors [brito2013conformal]. Following its geodesics with $\Lambda < 0$ in 2014, they found that a larger $|\Lambda|$ raises both the least and the greatest distance from the axis of a confined planar null geodesic, and that any negative constant unbinds some null geodesics confined at $\Lambda = 0$ [brito2014geodesics]. They found no trapped cylinders: every outgoing radial planar null geodesic escapes to infinity [brito2014geodesics]. With $\Lambda > 0$ they showed in 2015 that a large enough constant unbinds the planar timelike geodesics confined at $\Lambda = 0$ [brito2015geodesics]. They then replaced both singular ends, with an anisotropic fluid inside the field and a region of the Einstein static universe full of dust outside it, and built a static spacetime with no singularity [brito2015geodesics].¶Martín Richarte joined two copies of the cosmic string member with a positive constant across a cylindrical thin shell to form a wormhole in 2013 [richarte2013cylindrical]. Ernesto Eiroa and Claudio Simeone built wormholes from the negative constant family in 2015 and found that the matter at the throat has negative energy density [eiroa2015cylindrical]. The radially perturbed throats are unstable if they keep the static equations of state, and can be stable with a linearized relation between pressure and energy density [eiroa2015cylindrical]. S. Danial Forghani, Seyedhabibollah Mazharimousavi, and Mustafa Halilsoy joined black string members with different masses in 2019 and found radially stable wormholes for some equations of state [forghani2019cylindrical]. Jiří Veselý and Žofka matched magnetic interiors to unmagnetized exteriors of this family for both signs of the constant the same year, with a cylindrical shell of counter streaming charged particles between them [vesely2019magnetic]. Adam Tyc and Žofka returned to its geodesics in 2026, used the transformations of $\sigma$ that keep the form of the metric to confine $\sigma$ to values no greater than $1/2$, and concluded that its symmetry is toroidal [tyc2026geodesic].¶Jie Ren examined the negative constant family in 2016 as a gravitational dual to anisotropic quantum states, following null geodesics and calculating entanglement entropy, Wilson loops, and twopoint correlation functions [ren2016kasner]. David Kastor, Sourya Ray, and Jennie Traschen calculated the mass and spatial tensions of its higher dimensional form in 2017, and continued it to anisotropic Kasner cosmologies with a positive constant [kastor2017hair]. Gaurav Katoch, Ren, and Shubho Ranjan Roy calculated holographic complexity in the same four dimensional geometry in 2023 [katoch2023complexity]. They found a finite negative contribution from the singularity to the action, and a regulated volume that can lie on either side of the value for anti-de Sitter space [katoch2023complexity]. Fernando Ruiz Ruiz treated the timelike singularity as an inner boundary in 2026 and, with a Hamiltonian that includes that boundary, found a positive energy equal to the energy of the planar anti-de Sitter black hole [ruiz2026energy].¶Every member with $\Lambda \neq 0$ is of Petrov type I except those with $\sigma = -1/2$, $0$, $1/4$, $1/2$, and $1$, which are of type D and carry a fourth Killing vector [dasilva2000]. At $\sigma = 0$ that vector is a boost along the axis, and at $\sigma = \pm 1/2$ it is a rotation in the plane of $z$ and $\phi$, which gives those two members plane symmetry [dasilva2000, zofka2008]. With $\Lambda < 0$ the surface $\rho = 0$ of the member with $\sigma = 1/2$ is a horizon, and Žofka and Bičák transformed that member into the static, uncharged black string of José Lemos [dasilva2000, zofka2008, lemos1995]. Griffiths and Podolský found the member with $\sigma = 0$ to be a generalisation of the B III metric with a cosmological constant, among the solutions of Jerzy Plebański and Marek Demiański without expansion [griffiths2010linettian]. Gleiser found unstable modes of gravitational perturbations with a negative constant in 2017, for a large set of boundary conditions [gleiser2017stability]. With a positive constant he established the linear instability of the family in 2021 [gleiser2021perturbations].

related.text: At $\Lambda = 0$ both functions of the line element are the proper distance $\rho$, and the field is Tullio Levi-Civita's cylinder with $\sigma$ his mass parameter [dasilva2000, griffiths2010linettian].

With $\Lambda < 0$, $\sigma = 0$, and $C = 1$ the axis is regular and the field is the soliton of anti-de Sitter space, which William Bonnor called a second anti-de Sitter universe [sarioglu2009comment, bonnor2008second].

At $\Lambda = 0$ and $\sigma = 0$ the field is flat with an angular deficit about the axis, the cosmic string that Bernard Linet and Qingjun Tian set in a universe with a cosmological constant [griffiths2010linettian, zofka2008].
The flat member of these holes, the static black string of José Lemos, is the field with $\sigma = 1/2$ and $\Lambda < 0$, its horizon at $\rho = 0$ [zofka2008, lemos1995].
Written in horospherical coordinates, this black hole shares the leading terms of the field far from the axis when $\Lambda < 0$, and the radial dependence of its next terms [zofka2008].
Every member with $\Lambda < 0$ approaches anti-de Sitter space far from its axis, in horospherical coordinates [dasilva2000, zofka2008].

When $\Lambda > 0$, a toroidal region of the static universe full of dust can replace one of the two singular axes, and for small $\sigma$ the dust carries a mass per unit length close to $\sigma$ [griffiths2010linettian].

The member with $\sigma = 0$ is a generalisation of the B III metric with a cosmological constant, of type D and in the family of Jerzy Plebański and Marek Demiański without expansion [griffiths2010linettian].

coordinates.name: Toroidal
domains: \rho = 0 \;\text{(the axis, a curvature singularity unless } p_0\,p_2\,p_3 = 0\text{)}

parameters.description: Cosmological constant, positive here, an inverse length squared
Conicity about the axis $\rho = \pi/\sqrt{3\Lambda}$, an inverse length in the unit the powers are read in; with $\psi$ periodic in $2\pi$ it fixes the angular deficit there
Conicity, an inverse length in the unit the powers are read in; with $\phi$ periodic in $2\pi$ it fixes the angular deficit about the axis
Exponent along $t$, $p_0 = 2\sigma/\Sigma$, with $\sigma$ the mass parameter of Levi-Civita's cylinder and $\Sigma = 4\sigma^2 - 2\sigma + 1$
Exponent along $\phi$, $p_2 = (1 - 2\sigma)/\Sigma$
Exponent along $\psi$, $p_3 = 2\sigma(2\sigma - 1)/\Sigma$; the two conditions on the exponents leave one free
A length, close to $\rho$ near the axis and growing without bound as $\rho \to \pi/\sqrt{3\Lambda}$, with $dP/d\rho = 1 + 3\Lambda P^2/4$

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, \rho, \psi, \phi)$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time, $\rho$ the proper distance from the axis $\rho = 0$, a length, and $\psi$ and $\phi$ angles. The factor $(1 + 3\Lambda P^2/4)^{-2/3}$ is $\cos^{4/3}(\sqrt{3\Lambda}\,\rho/2)$, and we evaluate the powers of $P$ with $P$ in a fixed unit of length, so they are dimensionless. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.

parameters.description: Cosmological constant, of either sign, an inverse length squared
Conicity, an inverse length in the unit the powers are read in; with $\phi$ periodic in $2\pi$ it fixes the angular deficit about the axis
Exponent along $t$, $p_0 = 2\sigma/\Sigma$, with $\sigma$ the mass parameter of Levi-Civita's cylinder and $\Sigma = 4\sigma^2 - 2\sigma + 1$

Exponent along $z$, $p_3 = 2\sigma(2\sigma - 1)/\Sigma$; the two conditions on the exponents leave one free
An area, close to $y$ near the axis, with $dY/dy = (1 + \Lambda Y)^2$; for $\Lambda > 0$ it grows without bound as $y \to 1/\Lambda$

coordinates.convention: We use Gleiser's coordinates $(t, y, z, \phi)$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time, $z$ a length and $\Lambda y = \sin^2(\sqrt{3\Lambda}\,\rho/2)$, where $\rho$ is the proper distance from the axis, so that $t$, $z$, and $\phi/C$ are those of the proper distance charts multiplied by constants. We write the metric in $Y = y/(1 - \Lambda y)$ and evaluate its powers with $Y$ in a fixed unit of area, so they are dimensionless. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.

coordinates.convention: We use the coordinates $(t, r, z, \phi)$ of Sarıoğlu and Tekin, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time and $r$ and $z$ lengths, where $r = r_0\cosh^{2/3}(3\rho/2L)$ with $\rho$ the proper distance from the axis, so that $t$, $z$, and $\phi/C$ are those of the cylindrical chart multiplied by constants. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.
